name.description: As the books use it, including the article where the article is part of the name — 'the Others', 'the Administrator'.

kind.description: A people is a sapient species. A polity is anything that governs, organises or speaks for one — a state, a council, a movement, an enclave, a resistance. They share a register because in this series they are the same argument seen from two angles: who counts as a person, and who gets to decide.

of.description: For a polity, the id of the people whose polity it is. Omitted where the books leave it mixed or unstated — the UFS is deliberately not any one species'.

expansion.description: What an acronym or short name stands for, ONLY where a character expands it on the page. FAITH has no expansion field because the books never unpack it, and inventing a plausible one would be the exact failure this project exists to avoid.

place.description: World within that system, matching a `places` entry in systems.json.

status.description: extant = still going as of book 5. extinct = the species is gone. defunct = the polity is. unknown = the books don't say, which is a real answer.

contact.description: For a people: how it stands with the Bobs. This is the Prime Directive thread made into a field — 'uplifted' is Bob deciding that watching was also a choice, 'covert' is the Bobs walking among Quinlans without telling them, 'aware' is a people that knows and has its own opinion.

mentions.description: Re-derived from the corpus at validate time.

mentionPattern.description: Regex to count by, where the name alone is ambiguous. Required in practice for acronyms and common words: matching 'USE' case-insensitively finds the verb 286 times instead of the state 51 times, and 'the Others' finds the ordinary word. Case-sensitive unless the pattern says otherwise.

note.description: Our prose. Never quoted book text.

art.description: Filled by the build from assets/peoples/<id>.svg. Not hand-edited.
